3: //! Signal driver
4: 
5: use crate::io::driver::{Driver as IoDriver, Interest};
6: use crate::io::PollEvented;
7: use crate::park::Park;
8: use crate::signal::registry::globals;
9: 
10: use mio::net::UnixStream;
11: use std::io::{self, Read};
12: use std::ptr;
13: use std::sync::{Arc, Weak};
14: use std::task::{Context, Poll, RawWaker, RawWakerVTable, Waker};
15: use std::time::Duration;
16: 
17: /// Responsible for registering wakeups when an OS signal is received, and
18: /// subsequently dispatching notifications to any signal listeners as appropriate.
19: ///
20: /// Note: this driver relies on having an enabled IO driver in order to listen to
21: /// pipe write wakeups.
22: #[derive(Debug)]
23: pub(crate) struct Driver {
24:     /// Thread parker. The `Driver` park implementation delegates to this.
25:     park: IoDriver,
26: 
27:     /// A pipe for receiving wake events from the signal handler
28:     receiver: PollEvented<UnixStream>,
29: 
30:     /// Shared state
31:     inner: Arc<Inner>,
32: }
33: 
34: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
35: pub(crate) struct Handle {
36:     inner: Weak<Inner>,
37: }
38: 
39: #[derive(Debug)]
40: pub(super) struct Inner(());
41: 
42: // ===== impl Driver =====
43: 
44: impl Driver {
45:     /// Creates a new signal `Driver` instance that delegates wakeups to `park`.
46:     pub(crate) fn new(park: IoDriver) -> io::Result<Self> {
47:         use std::mem::ManuallyDrop;
48:         use std::os::unix::io::{AsRawFd, FromRawFd};
49: 
50:         // NB: We give each driver a "fresh" receiver file descriptor to avoid
51:         // the issues described in alexcrichton/tokio-process#42.
52:         //
53:         // In the past we would reuse the actual receiver file descriptor and
54:         // swallow any errors around double registration of the same descriptor.
55:         // I'm not sure if the second (failed) registration simply doesn't end
56:         // up receiving wake up notifications, or there could be some race
57:         // condition when consuming readiness events, but having distinct
58:         // descriptors for distinct PollEvented instances appears to mitigate
59:         // this.
60:         //
61:         // Unfortunately we cannot just use a single global PollEvented instance
62:         // either, since we can't compare Handles or assume they will always
63:         // point to the exact same reactor.
64:         //
65:         // Mio 0.7 removed `try_clone()` as an API due to unexpected behavior
66:         // with registering dups with the same reactor. In this case, duping is
67:         // safe as each dup is registered with separate reactors **and** we
68:         // only expect at least one dup to receive the notification.
69: 
70:         // Manually drop as we don't actually own this instance of UnixStream.
71:         let receiver_fd = globals().receiver.as_raw_fd();
72: 
73:         // safety: there is nothing unsafe about this, but the `from_raw_fd` fn is marked as unsafe.
74:         let original =
75:             ManuallyDrop::new(unsafe { std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::from_raw_fd(receiver_fd) });
76:         let receiver = UnixStream::from_std(original.try_clone()?);
77:         let receiver = park.new_with_interest_and_handle(
78:             receiver,
79:             Interest::READABLE | Interest::WRITABLE,
80:         )?;
81: 
82:         Ok(Self {
83:             park,
84:             receiver,
85:             inner: Arc::new(Inner(())),
86:         })
87:     }
88: 
89:     /// Returns a handle to this event loop which can be sent across threads
90:     /// and can be used as a proxy to the event loop itself.
91:     pub(crate) fn handle(&self) -> Handle {
92:         Handle {
93:             inner: Arc::downgrade(&self.inner),
94:         }
95:     }
96: 
97:     fn process(&self) {
98:         // Check if the pipe is ready to read and therefore has "woken" us up
99:         //
100:         // To do so, we will `poll_read_ready` with a noop waker, since we don't
101:         // need to actually be notified when read ready...
102:         let waker = unsafe { Waker::from_raw(RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)) };
103:         let mut cx = Context::from_waker(&waker);
104: 
105:         let ev = match self.receiver.registration().poll_read_ready(&mut cx) {
106:             Poll::Ready(Ok(ev)) => ev,
107:             Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => panic!("reactor gone: {}", e),
108:             Poll::Pending => return, // No wake has arrived, bail
109:         };
110: 
111:         // Drain the pipe completely so we can receive a new readiness event
112:         // if another signal has come in.
113:         let mut buf = [0; 128];
114:         loop {
115:             match (&*self.receiver).read(&mut buf) {
116:                 Ok(0) => panic!("EOF on self-pipe"),
117:                 Ok(_) => continue, // Keep reading
118:                 Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => break,
119:                 Err(e) => panic!("Bad read on self-pipe: {}", e),
120:             }
121:         }
122: 
123:         self.receiver.registration().clear_readiness(ev);
124: 
125:         // Broadcast any signals which were received
126:         globals().broadcast();
127:     }
128: }
129: 
130: impl IoDriver {
131:     pub(crate) fn new_with_interest_and_handle<E: mio::event::Source>(
132:         &self,
133:         mut io: E,
134:         interest: Interest,
135:     ) -> io::Result<PollEvented<E>> {
136:         use crate::io::driver::{Handle as IoHandle, Registration};
137: 
138:         let inner = &self.inner;
139: 
140:         let (address, shared) = {
141:             let io_dispatch = inner.io_dispatch.read().unwrap();
142:             if io_dispatch.is_shutdown {
143:                 return Err(io::Error::new(
144:                     io::ErrorKind::Other,
145:                     "failed to find event loop",
146:                 ));
147:             }
148:             match io_dispatch.allocator.allocate() {
149:                 Some(allocated) => allocated,
150:                 None => {
151:                     return Err(io::Error::new(
152:                         io::ErrorKind::Other,
153:                         "reactor at max registered I/O resources",
154:                     ));
155:                 }
156:             }
157:         };
158: 
159:         {
160:             let mut waiters = shared.waiters.lock();
161:             waiters.reader.take();
162:             waiters.writer.take();
163:         }
164: 
165:         let token = crate::io::driver::GENERATION.pack(
166:             shared.generation(),
167:             crate::io::driver::ADDRESS.pack(address.as_usize(), 0),
168:         );
169: 
170:         inner
171:             .registry
172:             .register(&mut io, mio::Token(token), interest.to_mio())?;
173: 
174:         inner.metrics.incr_fd_count();
175: 
176:         let registration = Registration {
177:             handle: IoHandle {
178:                 inner: Arc::clone(inner),
179:             },
180:             shared,
181:         };
182: 
183:         Ok(PollEvented {
184:             io: Some(io),
185:             registration,
186:         })
187:     }
188: }
189: 
190: const NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE: RawWakerVTable = RawWakerVTable::new(noop_clone, noop, noop, noop);
191: 
192: unsafe fn noop_clone(_data: *const ()) -> RawWaker {
193:     RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)
194: }
195: 
196: unsafe fn noop(_data: *const ()) {}
197: 
198: // ===== impl Park for Driver =====
199: 
200: impl Park for Driver {
201:     type Unpark = <IoDriver as Park>::Unpark;
202:     type Error = io::Error;
203: 
204:     fn unpark(&self) -> Self::Unpark {
205:         self.park.unpark()
206:     }
207: 
208:     fn park(&mut self) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
209:         self.park.park()?;
210:         self.process();
211:         Ok(())
212:     }
213: 
214:     fn park_timeout(&mut self, duration: Duration) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
215:         self.park.park_timeout(duration)?;
216:         self.process();
217:         Ok(())
218:     }
219: 
220:     fn shutdown(&mut self) {
221:         self.park.shutdown()
222:     }
223: }
224: 
225: // ===== impl Handle =====
226: 
227: impl Handle {
228:     pub(super) fn check_inner(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
229:         if self.inner.strong_count() > 0 {
230:             Ok(())
231:         } else {
232:             Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Other, "signal driver gone"))
233:         }
234:     }
235: }
236: 
237: cfg_rt! {
238:     impl Handle {
239:         /// Returns a handle to the current driver
240:         ///
241:         /// # Panics
242:         ///
243:         /// This function panics if there is no current signal driver set.
244:         #[track_caller]
245:         pub(super) fn current() -> Self {
246:             crate::runtime::context::signal_handle().expect(
247:                 "there is no signal driver running, must be called from the context of Tokio runtime",
248:             )
249:         }
250:     }
251: }
252: 
253: cfg_not_rt! {
254:     impl Handle {
255:         /// Returns a handle to the current driver
256:         ///
257:         /// # Panics
258:         ///
259:         /// This function panics if there is no current signal driver set.
260:         #[track_caller]
261:         pub(super) fn current() -> Self {
262:             panic!(
263:                 "there is no signal driver running, must be called from the context of Tokio runtime or with\
264:                 `rt` enabled.",
265:             )
266:         }
267:     }
268: }
